name: Stagalbog
summary: The Stagalbog is a dense, waterlogged marsh stretch across the southern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. Bordering the southern mountain range just below the Pool of Tears, it remains an untamed wilderness.

sections.title: The Southern Mire
sections.body: Stretching beneath the shadow of the southern crags, the Stagalbog is typical of the Swamp of Sorrows: stagnant water, drooping reeds, and tangled vegetation. It sits immediately south of the sunken ruins of the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, caught between the tainted lake and the rocky boundary of the region. Apart from rough wildlife, civilization has established no foothold here.

sections.title: Shadow of the Temple
sections.body: Because it borders the Pool of Tears, the Stagalbog frequently catches whatever shadows or corruptions seep from the Sunken Temple. While wind serpents have historically been absent from these bogs for generations, unnatural beasts and serpents tied to the Atal'ai priesthood often wander out of the deep marsh and lurk among the roots near Stagalbog Cave.

faq.answer: The Stagalbog is located in the southern part of the Swamp of Sorrows, situated directly south of the Pool of Tears and running along the base of the southern mountain range.

faq.q: What threats can be found wandering the bog?
faq.answer: The bog is inhabited by indigenous marsh beasts, predatory creatures, and unnatural horrors spilling over from the nearby Atal'ai temple complex in the Pool of Tears.

angles.text: The damp, sun-deprived roots of the Stagalbog provide prime growing conditions for swamp flora that thrive away from trodden paths.
The quiet swaths between the marsh water and the mountain cliffs make the Stagalbog a prime stalking ground for native swamp beasts and stray serpent whelps.
